looks to invest $5B in India over the next decade to expand its presence in the country, according to remarks at SEMICON India, the country's ‌flagship chip conference.

The investment will follow a three-pillar approach focused on deepening research and development in India, accelerating the semiconductor ecosystem and developing future talent, a company executive said, as per reports.

"Today, we are committing to a new 140-acre advanced semiconductor research park, bringing together cleanroom capabilities, engineering expertise, and collaborative R&D with customers and suppliers on one side," president of the semiconductor products group at Applied Materials, Prabu Raja said

"Second, accelerate the ecosystem in India. Inventions done here must scale globally. By 2035, we aim to grow our India-based supply chain capacity 10 times, creating opportunities for Indian suppliers and bringing global suppliers here..."

title: Applied Materials to invest $5B in India over the next decade
